Financeit est un fournisseur de financement au point de vente au service de certaines des plus grandes entreprises de rénovation domiciliaire et de commerce de détail au Canada. Notre plateforme aide les entreprises à conclure plus de ventes en offrant à leurs clients des options de paiements mensuels abordables pour leur prochain grand projet de rénovation, d'achat de véhicule ou de commerce de détail.
 Nous sommes une entreprise à taille humaine où vous pouvez avoir un réel impact interne, mais suffisamment grande pour faire la différence sur le marché. Chez Financeit, la collaboration, l'inclusion, l'équité et le respect ne sont pas de simples paroles en l'air, mais font partie intégrante de notre ADN. Si ce milieu de travail vous interpelle, nous espérons que vous vous joindrez à nous.
 À propos du rôle : 
 En mettant l'accent sur la croissance du volume de ventes au Québec, le ou la responsable régional(e) des ventes aura pour mission d'entretenir les comptes existants ainsi que de prospecter et qualifier de nouveaux clients potentiels.
 Relevant du directeur des ventes pour l'Est du Canada, ce rôle B2B consiste à gérer les relations avec nos marchands partenaires et à traiter directement avec les propriétaires, les directeurs financiers et les représentants d'entreprises du secteur de la rénovation domiciliaire désireuses d'utiliser notre plateforme de financement aux consommateurs.
 Nous recherchons une personne motivée par les défis et axée sur la performance, stimulée par le dépassement des objectifs. Vous êtes un(e) spécialiste de la prospection (un « chasseur » d'expérience) à l'aise avec les appels à froid, et vous comprenez que la signature du contrat n'est que le début du travail. Vous savez rester organisé(e) tout en travaillant à un rythme soutenu et en prêtant attention aux détails, sans jamais perdre de vue la vision globale et en plaçant le succès client au cœur de vos priorités.
 Le ou la responsable devra consacrer au moins 30 % de son temps sur le terrain, à démarcher de nouveaux clients potentiels et à interagir avec les marchands partenaires au sein de son territoire. Il s'agit d'un poste en télétravail, et la personne retenue doit résider au Québec et être en mesure de se déplacer sur l'ensemble du territoire.
 Vos responsabilités : 
 Développer, maintenir et gérer de solides relations avec nos marchands partenaires en effectuant au moins une rencontre en personne par mois par marchand.
 Générer et conclure de nouvelles opportunités d'affaires dans les secteurs de la rénovation domiciliaire.
 Réactiver les comptes sous-performants existants qui vous sont attribués dans votre territoire.
 Utiliser une connaissance approfondie des produits et des conseils en vente pour stimuler l'activité des marchands.
 Mettre à jour et accompagner régulièrement les partenaires sur le programme et les processus de Financeit.
 Enseigner aux entreprises comment utiliser notre suite d'outils pour positionner le financement et proposer des mensualités.
 Organiser et animer des séances de formation et d'accompagnement régulières auprès des marchands.
 Veiller au respect de nos exigences en matière d'approbation et de gestion des risques.
 Assurer un suivi rigoureux par l'entremise de rapports quotidiens et hebdomadaires sur l'ensemble de vos activités de vente.
 Produire des rapports, analyser les données, dégager les tendances et formuler des recommandations.
 Signaler les lacunes dans les processus et systèmes aux niveaux de gestion appropriés dès qu'elles sont détectées.
 S'efforcer d'atteindre les objectifs individuels et d'équipe sur une base mensuelle.
 Déplacements requis.
 Diplôme d'études collégiales (DEC), baccalauréat ou expérience pratique équivalente.
 5 ans ou plus d'expérience pratique en vente directe et en gestion de relations clients.
 2 ans ou plus d'expérience dans le domaine du prêt à la consommation, des logiciels SaaS ou de la rénovation domiciliaire.
 Excellente maîtrise du français et de l'anglais.
 Expertise démontrée dans la gestion réussie de relations de vente et de service B2B (un atout).
 Expérience de l'utilisation d'outils CRM, idéalement Salesforce.
 Excellentes compétences relationnelles et organisationnelles.
 Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités de front et à respecter des échéanciers serrés.
 Résider obligatoirement au Québec, Canada.

 Des événements virtuels tels que des dîners-conférences, fêtes d'entreprise, activités d'équipe ludiques et initiatives de bienfaisance.
 Des programmes d'apprentissage et de développement professionnel.

Nous célébrons la diversité des parcours et des perspectives, car nous savons qu'elle renforce notre équipe et améliore notre produit. Nous embauchons en fonction du talent, du potentiel et de la valeur ajoutée à notre culture : peu importe vos origines, votre identité ou votre parcours de vie, vous êtes le ou la bienvenu(e) ici.

Sous la supervision du Directeur exécutif, le titulaire du poste est responsable de supporter la force de vente et la clientèle dans la compréhension, la formation et l’utilisation de la gamme de produits sous sa responsabilité. Le titulaire du poste participe activement à l’élaboration du plan de développement des solutions et à la création des documents de développement de produits et des outils de prévente, d’après-vente et de mise en marché. Il assiste aussi le groupe d’ingénierie en effectuant des essais applicatifs sur les produits en développement et recommande des changements et des améliorations. Il contribue également à l’amélioration continue de la (ou les) ligne(s) de produits dont il est responsable. Finalement, il supporte le responsable de produits dans le développement de nouvelles solutions.
 Principales fonctions et responsabilités 
 Soutenir la force de vente et former les utilisateurs : 
 Identifier et développer de nouvelles solutions en tenant compte à la fois des capacités internes de développement, des solutions existantes sur le marché et des possibilités de partenariat
 Offrir et créer de la formation sur l’instrumentation et leurs applications pour la force de vente et les clients à l’international
 Contribuer à l’amélioration de la formation et des documents de formation.

 Analyser les besoins du marché et effectuer des recommandations quant aux produits et aux méthodes de vente

 Participer à la mise en marché : 
 Élaborer la documentation sur les produits/solutions et les outils de vente et d’après-vente selon les orientations fournies par le responsable de produits

Formation et expérience pertinente

 DEC en physique avec 8 à 10 ans d’expérience / Baccalauréat en physique avec 5 à 7 ans d’expérience ou combinaison pertinente équivalente, un atout;

 Chez Wabtec, ce n’est pas juste un emploi — c’est l’impact que vous créez. Quand nos gens se rassemblent, nous repoussons les limites du possible en améliorant continuellement ce que nous faisons et comment nous le faisons — pour nos clients et les uns pour les autres.

 Wabtec est un fournisseur mondial de premier plan d’équipements, de systèmes, de solutions numériques et de services à valeur ajoutée pour les secteurs ferroviaires de fret et de transport en commun. Forts de plus de 150 ans d’expérience, nous menons en matière de sécurité, d’efficacité, de fiabilité, d’innovation et de productivité. Nous bâtissons une culture où le leadership, l’inclusion et votre perspective unique alimentent le progrès.
 Nous sommes fiers d’être un employeur offrant l’égalité des chances. Nous accueillons les talents de tous les horizons, expériences et identités – y compris la race, le genre, l’âge, le handicap, le statut de vétéran et plus encore.

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.
 What is The Role 
 Elasticsearch powers search, observability, and AI retrieval (RAG) for the world's largest organizations. We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to join the Elasticsearch Performance team. In this role, you will lead architectural and code-level performance engineering initiatives. Your goal is to drive the continuous optimization and predictability of Elasticsearch performance, partnering with area-specific teams to unlock the full potential of our software.
 What You Will Be Doing 
 Owning core performance engineering initiatives from architecture to production, focusing on the delivery of high-impact optimizations. Leading the technical design, plan, and execution for major architectural and code-level performance improvements.
 Developing foundational performance models and methodologies for complex, distributed systems.
 Driving optimization strategies to ensure Elasticsearch remains performant, predictable, and scalable in diverse environments.
 Profiling and analyzing system behavior to identify bottlenecks in logging, metrics, vector search, and ES|QL.
 Ensuring robust performance benchmarks and regression detection for both stateful and stateless (Serverless) architectures.
 Collaborating across the company to embed performance-first thinking into new features from the outset.
 Drive automation efforts by designing and building AI-assisted optimization harnesses that streamline profiling, hypothesis testing, and benchmarking.
 Mentoring and coaching other engineers, fostering a culture of technical excellence and performance-aware development.
 What You Bring
 You have deep knowledge of Java internals and JVM memory management. You understand how concurrency models work. You can write code that is high-performance, thread-safe, and lock-free. This experience includes working with large open-source and enterprise codebases.
 You have proven experience in profiling and optimizing distributed systems. This includes deep experience with benchmarking tools (e.g.,flamegraphs, JMH, Rally), identifying performance regressions, and implementing algorithmic or hardware-aware optimizations.
 You have a solid comprehension of distributed systems architecture, including partition tolerance, cluster state propagation, and scaling challenges in large-scale data stores.
 You have a proven track record of using AI or advanced tooling to accelerate optimization, debug complex performance issues, and automate benchmarking workflows.
 You possess the ability to collaborate across functions and teams, acting as a force multiplier for performance engineering across the organization.
 You possess the ability to collaborate across functions and teams and seamlessly transition between different projects, codebases, or teams based on business priorities
 You can work autonomously, drive decisions and result in a distributed team by leveraging asynchronous, direct, and transparent communication.
 Bonus Points
 Experience integrating high-performance native libraries (e.g., C++, Rust, SIMD-accelerated code) into Java applications.
 Deep knowledge of modern storage engine performance, index modes, or vector search optimizations.
 Experience defining and managing Performance SLAs and success criteria for distributed systems.
 Experience working on the internals of a large-scale data store or search engine.
 Experience working on the internals of a data store or search engine.

À propos de GSK 
 Chez GSK, nous œuvrons à prévenir et à traiter les maladies grâce à la science, à la technologie et aux talents.

Nous investissons dans les technologies de pointe et dans l’amélioration continue de nos procédés afin de répondre aux défis liés à la fabrication de produits toujours plus complexes.
 À propos du poste 
 Le poste d’ Expert Standards LMSAT est un rôle d’expertise technique visant à assurer la maîtrise et la mise en œuvre efficace des standards techniques LMSAT sur le site.
 Selon son domaine d’expertise, la personne titulaire du poste agit comme référence technique pour un ou plusieurs standards, notamment :
 Le cycle de vie des produits et des procédés (PLM, étapes 1 à 3)
 La validation du nettoyage
 Le contrôle de la contamination, incluant la contamination microbienne, les particules physiques (PCCE) ainsi que les substances extractibles et lixiviables (E&L)
 L’inspection visuelle
 Les systèmes à usage unique (SUS)
 La personne titulaire du poste apporte son expertise aux équipes du site par l’accompagnement, le coaching, le partage des connaissances et l’orientation technique. Elle travaille dans un environnement matriciel et collabore étroitement avec les experts mondiaux LMSAT ainsi qu’avec les représentants des différents sites afin de partager les meilleures pratiques et de soutenir l’application cohérente des standards techniques.
 Vos principales responsabilités 
 Agir comme référence technique sur le site pour un ou plusieurs standards LMSAT relevant de son domaine d’expertise.
 Accompagner, encadrer et coacher les équipes du site en leur fournissant une expertise et un soutien technique adaptés.
 Renforcer les capacités et les connaissances du site dans les domaines techniques relevant des standards LMSAT.
 Contribuer à la définition, à l’évolution et à la mise en œuvre des standards techniques GSC, ainsi qu’au développement d’outils, de modèles et de lignes directrices.
 Participer activement aux communautés de pratique, groupes de travail et initiatives d’amélioration continue liés à son domaine d’expertise.
 Définir et soutenir la mise en place d’une gouvernance appropriée sur le site afin d’assurer l’application efficace des standards et la réalisation des projets d’amélioration associés.
 Développer et suivre des indicateurs de performance (KPI) afin de mesurer l’efficacité de la mise en œuvre des standards et d’identifier les opportunités d’amélioration.
 Identifier et faire remonter les enjeux ou difficultés rencontrés dans l’application des standards et contribuer à leur résolution.
 Collaborer avec les responsables mondiaux des standards LMSAT et les autres experts du site afin de soutenir les projets GSC, les initiatives d’amélioration continue et les projets stratégiques.
 Maintenir une connaissance à jour des exigences réglementaires, attentes d’inspection, standards de l’industrie, nouvelles technologies et risques liés à son domaine d’expertise.
 Pourquoi vous? 
 Diplôme universitaire dans une discipline scientifique, technique ou d’ingénierie.
 Minimum de 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle dans un domaine technique pertinent.
 Expérience dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : Validation ou vérification du nettoyage;
 Cycle de vie de la validation des procédés (étapes 1 à 3);
 Contrôle de la contamination, incluant PCCE, E&L et contamination microbienne;
 Inspection visuelle;
 Systèmes à usage unique (SUS).
 Expérience au sein d’équipes multidisciplinaires et dans un environnement matriciel.
 Connaissances en gestion des risques et gestion de projets.
 Bonne connaissance des exigences réglementaires applicables à son domaine d’expertise.
 Excellentes aptitudes en rédaction technique et en communication.
 Capacité à influencer, à collaborer et à travailler efficacement avec des parties prenantes à différents niveaux de l’organisation.
 Autonomie, proactivité et attitude positive et constructive.
 Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités, à organiser son travail et à respecter les échéanciers.
 Capacité à travailler avec précision dans un environnement où les priorités peuvent évoluer.
 Anglais avancé, à l’oral comme à l’écrit.
 Mode de travail 
 Ce poste est offert en mode hybride, conformément à la politique RH interne en matière de télétravail. Vous serez basé(e) à Sainte-Foy, Québec, avec une présence régulière sur le site et sur le terrain afin de collaborer avec les équipes, soutenir les activités techniques et participer aux rencontres, validations et autres activités nécessitant une présence sur place.
 À quoi ressemble la réussite dans ce rôle? 
 Les standards techniques LMSAT sont compris, adoptés et appliqués efficacement sur le site.
 Les équipes disposent du soutien et de l’expertise nécessaires pour appliquer les standards de façon cohérente.
 Les enjeux liés à la mise en œuvre des standards sont identifiés rapidement et font l’objet d’un suivi approprié.
 Les bonnes pratiques sont partagées efficacement entre le site, les autres sites GSC et les experts mondiaux.
 Les indicateurs de performance permettent de mesurer les progrès et de soutenir l’amélioration continue.
 Les initiatives et projets liés aux standards LMSAT sont réalisés dans le respect des exigences de qualité, réglementaires et opérationnelles.

Allier science, technologie et talent pour vaincre ensemble la maladie.

About Valsoft 
 Valsoft builds and scales vertical market software companies. We partner with strong teams, invest in the long term, and run disciplined operating systems to drive sustainable growth across our portfolio.
 About BluSynq 
 BluSynq is changing the way operators run their front desk. Our AI-powered agent connects to the tools a business already uses and answers questions, books appointments and closes deals — automatically, 24/7 — over voice, text and email. We are a fast-scaling, tech-driven business inside the Valsoft / Aspire Software portfolio, working closely with DockMaster, the leading marina management platform.
 The Opportunity 
 This is a first or second sales job, and a real one. 
 We're hiring a Junior Account Executive to take BluSynq into new markets.
 BluSynq already has a natural home inside DockMaster's marina customer base. That is not your territory. Yours is everything outside it: independent operators who have never heard of us, and the adjacent industries where the same problem exists. If a business loses money every time the phone rings and nobody picks up, it's a prospect.
 You won't be doing it alone. A dedicated Sales Development Representative works alongside you, building target lists and running first-touch outreach to book qualified meetings into your calendar. From that first meeting on, the deal is yours: discovery, demo, proposal, negotiation and close.
 You'll still create pipeline of your own. The best sellers always do, and in a new market a rep who only works booked meetings never learns why the market says no. But you have a partner at the top of the funnel, and a real say in who they call.
 You will not be building the go-to-market strategy. That's the point. The talk tracks, demo flow, pricing and CRM process are being built for you by the senior seller and the COO. What you will do is find out which industries outside our home market actually buy — and that read is worth as much to us as the revenue.
 You'll be coached directly, weekly, on live calls and recorded ones. If you're hungry, coachable and willing to pick up the phone yourself when the calendar looks thin, this is a seat where you can be closing your own deals inside 60 days and running a full territory inside a year.
 Where You'll Sell 
 Every deal you close is a net-new logo. You'll work two fronts:
 •       The marine market we don't already serve — independent marinas, boatyards, yacht clubs, waterfront venues and dealerships that are not DockMaster customers.
 •       Adjacent industries with the same front-desk problem — appointment-driven, phone-dependent, owner-operated businesses, including:
 –       RV parks, campgrounds and glamping sites
 –       Self-storage and boat/RV storage facilities
 –       Marine and powersports dealerships and their service departments
 –       Entertainment attractions, waterparks and event venues
 –       Home and field services — HVAC, plumbing, landscaping, pool service
 –       Auto service and repair shops
 –       Clinics, veterinary practices, salons and spas
 Part of the job is proving which of these are real. You and your SDR will run structured tests in new verticals, two at a time, and report back on what lands and what doesn't. Any prospect that turns out to be a DockMaster customer gets routed to the DockMaster team — those accounts are covered separately, and the rules of engagement will be written down for you before day one.
 What You'll Do 
 Work with your SDR to open new markets 
 •       Partner daily with your SDR: agree the target account criteria, review the lists they build in ZoomInfo and LinkedIn, listen to their calls, and tell them what is landing so the meetings get better.
 •       Accept, qualify or reject every meeting they book against criteria you have both signed up to — with feedback either way, same day. That loop is how the top of the funnel improves.
 •       Self-source a meaningful share of your own pipeline — phone, email, LinkedIn and the occasional trade show — so you are never dependent on someone else's calendar.
 •       Research every account before the call, so the first 20 seconds are about their business and not about us.
 •       Learn a new industry's vocabulary fast enough to sound credible to an operator who has run that business for twenty years.
 •       Log every touch in HubSpot the same day, tagged by vertical and lead source. Clean CRM is how we tell a good market from a bad one, and SDR-sourced from self-sourced.
 Own the sales cycle 
 •       Own every deal from the first meeting to signature. Once a lead is handed to you, it is yours — the forecast, the follow-up and the outcome.
 •       Run discovery calls using our qualification framework, and get to the operator's actual problem: missed calls, after-hours bookings, staff time lost to the phone.
 •       Deliver the BluSynq demo and connect what the prospect just heard to time saved and revenue captured.
 •       Build and send proposals, handle standard objections, and close.
 •       Hand new customers to Onboarding and Customer Success cleanly, with the context they need to get the customer live fast.
 Report back and get better every week 
 •       Come to your 1:1 with your numbers, your recorded calls and the one thing you want to fix.
 •       Give a clear read on each vertical you test: who answered, what landed, what they pushed back on, whether it's worth more of our time.
 •       Feed real objections, competitive mentions and pricing pushback back to the team so the playbook improves.
 •       Contribute to talk tracks and sequences once you've earned an opinion by making the calls.
 Ramp and Expectations 
 First 30 days — learn the product and pick your ground 
 •       Certified on the BluSynq demo and able to deliver it unassisted.
 •       Two target verticals agreed with the COO and your SDR, with lists built and outbound live in both.
 •       A working rhythm established with your SDR: shared qualification criteria, a weekly list review and a same-day feedback loop on every meeting booked.
 •       HubSpot hygiene at 100%: every activity logged, every next step dated, every account tagged by vertical.
 Days 31–60 — run the cycle 
 •       Consistently hitting weekly activity targets and holding a live discovery calendar.
 •       Running your own demos and building qualified pipeline in both test verticals.
 •       Converting SDR-booked meetings at or above our benchmark, with self-sourced opportunities on top.
 •       First closed deal on the board.
 •       An early, evidence-based read on which of the two verticals is responding.
 Days 61–90 — carry a number 
 •       Full quota carrying, with 3x pipeline coverage against it.
 •       A repeatable weekly rhythm: SDR review, self-sourced prospecting, discover, demo, propose, close.
 •       Hitting the agreed self-sourced share of pipeline alongside SDR-sourced volume.
 •       A documented view of which verticals convert, which to drop, and a third in test.
 •       Forecasting your own deals accurately enough that we can plan around them.
 KPIs you'll be measured on 
 •       Discovery calls held per week at full ramp: 8–10 across SDR-booked and self-sourced.
 •       Self-sourced outbound activity: ~25 quality touches a day, including live cold dials.
 •       Share of your pipeline you sourced yourself, against a ratio agreed in week one.
 •       Speed and quality of your feedback loop with the SDR — every booked meeting dispositioned same day.
 •       New-logo closes and new ARR — all of it net-new, none of it from the DockMaster base.
 •       Demo-to-close conversion against a team benchmark you'll be given in week one.
 •       Verticals tested per quarter, with a written read on each.
 •       Pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy and CRM data quality.
 What We're Looking For 
 Required 
 •       0–2 years of experience in a sales, customer-facing or target-driven role. A first sales job is welcome.
 •       Genuinely comfortable making a cold call — no referral, no inbound form, no existing relationship.
 •       Resilient about rejection, because opening a new market means a lot of it before the first yes.
 •       Clear, confident communicator — on the phone, on video and in writing.
 •       Coachable: you take feedback, apply it the same week, and ask for more.
 •       Willing to be a partner to your SDR rather than a passenger — giving them direction and feedback, not just taking their meetings.
 •       Organised and self-directed enough to run your own day in a remote role without someone counting your hours.
 •       Curious about how different kinds of businesses actually operate, and interested in getting good at software sales as a craft.
 •       Legally able to work in Canada and available to work North American business hours.
 Preferred 
 •       Any exposure to cold outbound — SDR/BDR work, retail, hospitality, call centre, recruiting, fundraising, or another role where you had a number and a script.
 •       Experience selling into more than one industry, or into small owner-operated businesses where the buyer is the owner.
 •       Experience with a CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce or similar) and prospecting tools like ZoomInfo — helpful, not required. We'll teach it.
 •       Familiarity with marinas, boating, RV parks, campgrounds, storage, dealerships or another owner-operator business. Knowing the customer is worth more here than knowing SaaS.
 •       Interest in AI and automation, and the ability to explain it to someone who doesn't care how it works — only what it does for them.
 What We're Not Asking For 
 •       SaaS experience. We'd rather have a fast learner with the right instincts than someone with three years of bad habits.
 •       A university degree in anything specific.
 •       An existing book of business or industry contacts.
 Why Join 
 •       You're not farming someone else's customer list. Every logo you close is a new one.
 •       You have a dedicated SDR feeding the top of your funnel from day one — rare in a first AE seat — and you own the deal from the first meeting onward.
 •       Sell a product prospects can hear working in the first two minutes of a demo, in markets that haven't been called on yet.
 •       Real influence in your first year on which industries BluSynq goes after next — your data decides it.
 •       Short sales cycles: you'll get more at-bats in a year here than in three years selling enterprise software, which is how sellers actually get good.
 •       Direct, weekly coaching from a senior seller and the COO — not a 40-person SDR floor.
 •       A defined path: this seat is built to grow into a full Account Executive territory, with clear milestones rather than a vague promise.
 •       Competitive base salary with uncapped commission.
 •       Backed by Valsoft / Aspire Software — the stability of a global portfolio with the pace and ownership of a startup.

Since 2015, Mejuri has reimagined what fine jewelry can be in a modern world—shifting it from a traditional gift to to a personal choice rooted in self-expression.
 Founded by third-generation jeweller Noura Sakkijha, the brand was built on a simple idea: fine jewelry shouldn’t require a special occasion, and it should never come with guilt. It’s about celebrating yourself—your style, your life, your everyday.
 Mejuri meets customers where they are—online, in app, and through a growing global retail footprint of 58+ stores worldwide. Mejuri is also deeply committed to doing things the right way, with responsible sourcing, sustainable practices, and philanthropic initiatives that reflect our values and long-term vision.
 Job Overview 
 The Senior Demand Planner owns the unit sales forecast and the receipt need that flows from it, end to end, across an assigned set of pillars and collections. You build the bottom-up forecast at the geography level and translate it into the monthly receipt need that buying decisions are built on — and you're accountable for both the accuracy of that forecast and the judgment behind it.
 You drive the demand side of the monthly S&OP cycle: presenting your forecast and receipt need at the monthly consensus meeting, walking senior leadership through your assumptions at S&OP, and speaking to any style in your portfolio at a granular level in the weekly trading meeting. Your forecast brings together customer insights, product strategy, market trends, and operational constraints into one coherent demand plan.
 Demand in jewelry moves with gifting moments, cultural trends, and input costs that shift with the market — the forecast you own changes shape with it throughout the year.
 What you'll do 
 Own the unit sales forecast: Build and maintain a rolling monthly unit forecast at style/color level over a 12–18 month horizon — built net of returns at geography level, and rolled up to total so that aggregate performance never masks a market-level imbalance. Overlay known business drivers from the shared planning calendar: promotions, campaigns, launches, store openings, and key trading periods.
 Translate demand into a receipt dollar need: Convert the unit forecast into the monthly receipt dollar need that Merchandise Planning stress-tests against open-to-buy, and bring it to the consensus meeting with a defensible number and a clear point of view on the trade-offs.
 Manage inventory coverage targets: Own network-level weeks-of-supply and safety stock targets in alignment with Merchandise Planning’s turn goals and Allocation’s in-store average inventory needs, and shape monthly receipts to the seasonal demand curve.
 Drive the monthly S&OP cycle: Own the demand inputs and cadence of the monthly planning cycle — actualizing the prior month, reforecasting on real selling signals, leading the demand consensus meeting, presenting your plan at monthly S&OP, and delivering the locked forecast, weekly disaggregation, and receipt plan on time every cycle.
 Own size distribution curves: Build and maintain the optimal size distribution for every sized style, and recalibrate as the assortment evolves.
 Own forecast accuracy and forecast health: Track actuals against plan at style/color level, distinguishing genuine demand shifts from supply-constrained misses before revising anything downward. Measure both forecast accuracy and directional bias, root-cause the misses that matter, and turn what you learn into a methodology change rather than a one-off correction.
 Forecast across the style lifecycle: Take new introductions from handoff through their first selling period, and carry styles through growth, peak, maturity, and exit with the right forecast and inventory posture at each stage.
 Partner with Supply on inventory risk: Work with Supply as a two-way early warning system on excess, stockouts, delivery delays, and quality issues — aligning on root cause together before adjusting the plan, and adapting the forecast and receipt need when the supply picture changes.
 Make the process better: Continuously evaluate and improve our demand planning process — sharper methodology, better tooling, less manual rebuilding, and planner time spent where judgment actually adds value.
 We're building an AI-fluent organization. We welcome candidates at all stages of their AI journey — what matters is curiosity, a willingness to learn, and an openness to working alongside AI tools as part of how we do our best work.
 What you'll bring to the team 
 3–5 years of experience in demand planning, merchandise planning, inventory planning, or retail analytics within a fast-paced retail, DTC, or e-commerce environment — with meaningful time spent owning a forecast, not only reporting on one.
 Strong command of forecasting methodology — baseline and trend construction, seasonal shape curves, comp-style logic, promotional overlays, and safety stock and coverage models — and the judgment to know when a forecast needs adjusting, and by how much.
 Experience operating inside an S&OP or monthly consensus process — building a geo-level plan, presenting it to senior stakeholders, and holding a point of view under challenge.
 Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication — aligning Merchandising, Merchandise Planning, Commercial, Marketing, Finance, Allocation, and Supply partners around one plan even when their inputs conflict, and making complex quantitative work land clearly with non-analytical audiences.
 High ownership, rigour, and a continuous improvement mindset — always looking for a better way to run the process, and comfortable operating at pace as priorities shift.
 Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, and comfort working in a demand planning system and a BI tool to build your own analysis without waiting on someone else’s queue. Experience with SQL is an asset.
 Experience in jewelry, accessories, or another category with sized, personalized, or attribute-driven product is considered a strong asset, as is experience implementing or materially improving a demand planning system.
 Enthusiasm for Mejuri’s mission and the customers we serve.
 Benefits at Mejuri:

 A hybrid work model for all corporate roles

 We are looking for experienced and safety-focused Test Drivers to support a road data collection project focused on capturing information about road signs, traffic lights, and other road infrastructure.
 Drivers will operate a project vehicle along predefined routes and collect high-quality data using specialized equipment installed in the vehicle.
Key Responsibilities: Drive assigned routes according to the daily schedule and project instructions.
 Collect data on road signs, traffic lights, road markings, and other relevant road infrastructure.
 Operate and monitor data collection equipment throughout each shift.
 Follow predefined routes accurately and comply with all project procedures.
 Drive safely in a variety of weather and road conditions, including:
 Sunny and low-sun conditions
 Rain and cloudy weather
 Fog
 Snow and snow-covered roads
 Check equipment and data collection setup before and after each shift.
 Safely handle and transfer project SSDs and other equipment as required.
 Send collected SSDs to the Operations Lead after each shift, following the established project process.
 Report any equipment issues, route deviations, incidents, or data collection problems promptly.

 Clean criminal/background check.

 Ability to follow detailed instructions and predefined routes.
 Comfortable working with technical equipment and basic digital tools.

We’re looking for a Staff Product Manager to lead the enterprise readiness and platform modernization strategy for SaaS Manager, 1Password’s product for helping organizations discover, understand, and govern the applications their employees use. You’ll shape a multi-quarter roadmap across data ingestion, integrations, reliability, admin experiences, and responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities, connecting deep technical decisions to customer and business outcomes. Reporting to the Director of Product, SaaS Manager, this remote role is open to candidates based in the United States or Canada.



How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



What we're looking for:

• 8+ years of product management experience, including end-to-end strategy and roadmap ownership for Business-to-Business (B2B) Software as a Service (SaaS) products.

• Technical fluency with integrations, application programming interfaces (APIs), data pipelines, platform architecture, and the trade-offs involved in building for enterprise scale.

• Experience leading complex, multi-quarter initiatives across Product, Engineering, Design, Security, Privacy, and other cross-functional teams.

•  Strong product discovery, problem framing, iterative validation, prioritization, and success measurement skills.

• Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain recommendations, trade-offs, and risks to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Experience with SaaS management, license management, IT asset management, identity and access management, cybersecurity, or other technically complex enterprise products.

• Experience with third-party SaaS ecosystems, including single sign-on (SSO), System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), OAuth, audit logs, or similar integration patterns, as well as responsible AI-assisted product development.

• Own the product strategy, roadmap, and prioritization for SaaS Manager’s platform modernization and enterprise readiness initiatives.

• Lead discovery with customers, internal partners, and data to identify the highest-impact enterprise problems and workflows.

• Partner with Engineering and Design to evaluate architecture options, clarify requirements, and translate complex problems into shippable milestones.

• Define success metrics and work with Product Analytics and Data partners to measure reliability, adoption, customer impact, and business outcomes.

• Align multiple Product and Engineering teams around priorities, decisions, dependencies, and delivery risks.

 The Staff Product Security Engineer Opportunity 
 As a Staff Product Security Engineer, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Okta’s products by conducting comprehensive security reviews, guiding engineering teams in secure development practices, and handling externally reported vulnerabilities. You will engage in code reviews, penetration testing, and architectural security assessments to ensure the security of Okta’s platforms and features.
 This role is not suited for individuals who rely solely on automated vulnerability scanning. Instead, you must possess a deep technical understanding of web applications, backend services, penetration testing methodologies, and secure design principles.
 A successful candidate will have expertise in authentication protocols (SAML, OAuth, OIDC), threat modeling, and a strong desire to automate security processes by building tools that proactively identify vulnerabilities. You will also be responsible for communicating risks, impact, and remediation strategies to developers, leadership, and external audiences through documentation, presentations, and external publications. The ideal candidate will also demonstrate a deep technical background in assessing AI-integrated software architectures and securing Large Language Models (LLMs) against emerging threats and modern vulnerability classes.

 What You Will Do 
 Conduct security reviews, including design reviews, threat modeling, and penetration testing of new features and major changes.
 Perform manual secure code reviews across multiple programming languages.
 Identify and mitigate security vulnerabilities, providing clear guidance to engineering teams.
 Lead product security incidents, assess risks, and drive remediation efforts.

 Mentor junior engineers and provide guidance to non-security staff on secure development practices.
 Represent Okta externally through security research, conference talks, and publications.
 What You Bring

 Strong experience in penetration testing and secure development practices.
 Deep technical background in assessing Large Language Models (LLMs) and securing AI-integrated software architectures.
 Proficiency in multiple programming languages (e.g., Java, Go, Python, C/C++).
 Deep understanding of authentication & authorization protocols (OIDC, SAML, OAuth).
 Strong communication skills to explain risks and remediation to developers and leadership.

 Experience leading security incidents and risk assessments.

KittySpout / DoggySpout is looking for a hungry Junior Media Buyer to join our team! You will launch every approved ad fast and right, and manage budgets, campaigns and ads across Facebook, Google, AppLovin, TikTok and Snapchat, following our SOPs. This is a growth seat: you work directly with our Head of Growth and learn from them day in, day out.
 We spend $2,500,000+ per month on paid media , so you'll get more reps in a month than most buyers get in a year. We are looking to hire someone with 1–3 years of Meta media buying, with Facebook as their main specialty. The ideal candidate is hungry, humble, gets the details right every time, and wants to grow from Junior Media Buyer to Media Buyer, Senior Media Buyer and Head of Paid/Growth.
 The mission of this role
 Launch every approved ad fast and right, and manage budgets, campaigns and ads across Facebook, Google, AppLovin, TikTok and Snapchat (about $2.5M+ a month), following our SOPs. Success is ads live within 24 hours, budgets surfed and scaled through the day, and spend and CPA targets hit consistently. The path is Junior Media Buyer → Media Buyer → Senior Media Buyer → Head of Paid/Growth, earned by consistently hitting spend and CPA targets.
 Who are we?
 KittySpout is a premium DTC brand selling stainless steel cat water fountains, filters and accessories. We sell across Shopify, Amazon and Chewy, and we're one of the fastest-growing brands in the pet space – $50M+ in annual revenue and scaling to $100M+. We recently launched DoggySpout, expanding into an entirely new vertical and customer base. We're a 100% remote, lean, senior team that moves fast, and every person here has a massive impact on the business.
 What is our culture like & who is a good fit?
 Culture-fit is our #1 factor when hiring! We have a genuine will-to-win. No work is beneath us if it moves us towards our goals. We use creativity to do more with less – and quickly. We use data to make decisions and live by four core values:
 Better Everyday – improve one thing in the buying process each week and write it into the SOPs.
 Speed Is King – launch within 24 hours, and check and scale budgets every couple of hours.
 Work Smart – AI and automation first. Use AdManage, Claude and automations for launching and admin, and spot tasks that can be automated.
 Overdeliver – bring the Head of Growth the problem and the fix before being asked.
 If you want a stress-free corporate 9–5 job, this isn't it. 
 If you want to challenge yourself and shape a fast-growing company, work directly with the founder, and play a big role in scaling it to $100M+... If you want to drive results with a group of passionate, smart, hardworking people, in an environment without politics or corporate chicanery, being hands-on and active – then you've come to the right place.
 Outcomes (what success looks like)
 90-day targets for each outcome are agreed with you before your start date.
 Approved ads launch within 24 hours, correctly named and formatted – time from strategist handover to live (Asana, AdManage)
 Budgets are surfed and scaled every couple of hours across every channel – spend pacing vs plan by channel (ad platforms, Northbeam)
 Ads and campaigns are optimised daily and spend and CPA targets are hit consistently – spend vs plan and nCPA by channel (Northbeam)
 Every account is checked daily and big changes are logged – daily account check, Northbeam comments log
 Media buying processes are written down – SOPs written and kept up to date, so daily admin can be delegated or automated
 Key Objectives
 Launch approved ads, Trybe creator ads, landing pages and funnel tests every day – on time and launch-ready.
 Manage budgets, campaigns and ads across Facebook, Google, AppLovin, TikTok and Snapchat.
 Surf and scale budgets every couple of hours, and run the daily budget reset at about 2am EST.
 Check every ad account daily in Northbeam, optimise to our SOPs and log big changes.
 Write and improve our media buying SOPs so daily admin can be delegated or automated.
 Learn from the Head of Growth every week and apply the feedback the next day.
 Fully remote, full-time
 Fluent in English
 Meta Media Buying: About 2 years (1–3) of hands-on Meta media buying is a must – Facebook is your main specialty and you understand it well.
 Time Zone & Availability: Available at about 2am EST for the daily budget reset.
 Attention to Detail: You get naming and formatting right every time.
 Reliable: You do the daily checks and budget resets every day, without being chased.
 Ready to Learn: You learn quickly, ask for the why behind each decision, take feedback well and apply it the next day. No ego.
 Long-Term Mindset: You want to work side by side with a senior buyer and see this as the start of a path to Head of Paid/Growth.
 Tools: Comfortable with Meta Ads Manager, and quick to pick up AdManage, Northbeam, Asana and AI tools like Claude.
 No issue working overtime or on the weekends if needed. You are passionate about your work.
 Excellent cultural fit as per our values above.

 Accountabilities

We are seeking a strategic, collaborative and product-minded leader to join our team as Assistant Vice President (AVP), Enterprise Digital Capabilities. This role is a key leader in Manulife's multi-year transformation to modernize and converge our digital ecosystem across Canada, the US, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.
At the heart of this role is a simple objective: identify what is common across our digital experiences, build it once as an enterprise capability, and enable markets and segments to reuse and extend it to accelerate their own digital roadmaps.
Manulife has established a strong portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities that support our Digital Storefront transformation and broader unification ambitions. The next opportunity is to expand and scale this portfolio to accelerate the unification strategies and roadmaps of our segments and advance One Manulife experiences across the enterprise. The AVP will lead this evolution – working across segments to identify where common capabilities can create the greatest incremental value, bringing together requirements to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise reuse, defining adoption and rollout strategies, and establishing a federated model where capabilities can be developed globally or contributed by segments and scaled for broader enterprise benefit.
The AVP will own the strategy and evolution of this portfolio — identifying new opportunities for reuse, prioritizing investment, establishing strong product management disciplines, driving adoption, optimizing existing capabilities and ensuring that each enterprise investment continues to deliver measurable value.
A critical part of the role is leading the Common Capability Collective, bringing together digital and product leaders from across the enterprise to identify common needs, align roadmaps, determine where enterprise investment can eliminate duplication and accelerate delivery, and create a shared view of capability priorities.
This is an enablement role, not ownership of individual market or segment experiences. The AVP will partner closely with Digital Storefront and segment digital leaders to understand their roadmaps and determine how enterprise capabilities can help them deliver faster, with greater quality, consistency and efficiency.
The AVP will operate in a two-in-a-box partnership with a complementary Global Technology leader, jointly shaping the business and technology evolution of enterprise digital capabilities. Together, they will ensure capabilities are scalable, secure, reusable, well-integrated and designed for long-term enterprise value.

 Enterprise Capability Strategy & Portfolio 
 Own the strategy, roadmap and ongoing evolution of Manulife's portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities.
 Establish a clear view of the capabilities required to support digital convergence across markets, segments and channels.
 Continuously identify common business and customer needs that can be solved once and reused across the enterprise.
 Assess existing segment capabilities for opportunities to scale them globally rather than rebuilding equivalent solutions.

 Maintain a multi-year capability roadmap aligned to Digital Storefront, segment roadmaps and Manulife's broader digital strategy.

 Common Capability Collective & Federated Leadership 
 Lead the Common Capability Collective, bringing together Digital Storefront and product leaders from across the enterprise to jointly shape capability priorities and investment.
 Create transparency across segment roadmaps to identify shared needs, opportunities for reuse and potential duplication before investment occurs.
 Establish a federated model that enables capabilities to originate within segments where appropriate and subsequently evolve into reusable enterprise capabilities.
 Build alignment around enterprise standards and shared capabilities while preserving segment accountability for their own customer experiences and business outcomes.
 Create clear decision rights, funding principles, ownership models and governance for the creation and evolution of common capabilities.
 Product Management & Capability Evolution 
 Establish strong product management disciplines across the enterprise capability portfolio, including product vision, roadmaps, adoption, performance measurement and lifecycle management.
 Ensure every capability has clear customer and business outcomes, ownership, success measures and an evolution roadmap.
 Use segment feedback, performance data and emerging customer needs to continuously improve capabilities.

 AI Enablement & Optimization

 Identify opportunities to embed AI directly into capabilities to improve customer experiences, decisioning, personalization and digital effectiveness.
 Apply AI and automation across the capability lifecycle to accelerate development, testing, implementation, operations and ongoing optimization.

 Establish clear onboarding, documentation, implementation patterns and support models that make enterprise capabilities easy for teams to adopt.
 Build awareness and understanding of available capabilities across the organization to increase reuse and prevent unnecessary reinvention.

 Champion a culture of reuse and enterprise thinking while recognizing the differentiated needs of individual markets and businesses.

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. GROWTH STRATEGY

 - Own the growth thesis for 1Password's AI opportunities, covering the customer segments we target, the outcomes we deliver that we win on, and the workflows we get embedded into. Revise it as evidence arrives from customers, partners, and the market.

 About the role 
 US Off-Price is a fast, reactive production book of licensed off-price programs shipped to club, mass and off-price retail. It runs high volumes across many factories and countries, on compressed timelines, with a heavy colour, packaging and compliance load and little room for error. The Production Manager takes senior operating ownership of this book, is the person who solves the day-to-day problems so they stop escalating to the Director, and grows into fuller ownership of sourcing, costing, governance and continuous improvement. The role frees the Director to focus on strategy, vendors and growth, and creates the coverage and redundancy the team currently lacks, so that no brand or book depends on a single person.
 Core responsibilities 
 Own from day one. 
 Own production end to end.  Take full operational ownership of the US Off-Price book from PO through delivery, drive the critical path, and be the person who solves problems and manages issues to resolution rather than passing them up.
 Manage the overseas factory base.  Own the day-to-day relationship and performance of factories across Pakistan, India, China, Cambodia and others: capacity, lead times, execution, issues and escalations.
 Oversee QC, inspection, testing and compliance.  Overlook the QCs and inspection reports, and ensure testing, regulatory and brand compliance, and importer and licensing documentation are all up to the mark.
 Drive shipments out.  Ensure goods ship on time, manage bookings and logistics, and clear blockers before they hit ex-factory and ship dates.
 Keep the system reflecting reality.  Ensure BlueCherry is always up to date with the real, current scenario: accurate POs, styles, BOMs, ex-factory and ship dates, and status, so the WIP is reliable for the whole business.
 Own the weekly cross-functional update.  Provide a clear weekly status update to Commercial, Shipping and Operations so the wider business works from one reliable view of the book.
 Be the coverage layer.  Step in and carry a coordinator's book when they are out, including backstopping the largest accounts, so absences no longer double the next day's work or land on the Director.
 Develop over the first 6 to 12 months. 
 Governance and KPI tracking.  Build and own the KPIs that run the book (on-time delivery, past-due, lead time, cost variance, factory scorecards, compliance status), track them, and report against them to drive accountability across the team and the factory base.
 Systems and tools for continuous improvement.  Develop dashboards, trackers and automation, including AI where useful, to cut manual work, surface issues early, and continuously improve how the team and the book run.
 Develop the team.  Give senior day-to-day guidance to a relatively junior coordinator group, raising their consistency and ownership over time.

 We are seeking a Data Scientist, Risk Analytics & Modeling, to work under the direction of the Director - Risk Analytics, Data Science & Reporting to develop and deliver robust risk machine learning and statistical models that support better credit decision-making, portfolio management, and risk measurement. You will play a key role in developing IFRS 9 models, behavioural models, and other predictive risk solutions, while building new modelling capabilities, operationalising and automating analytical processes, and turning complex data into actionable insights for stakeholders across the business.

 What you’ll be doing: 
 Build, validate, and refine sophisticated risk machine learning and statistical models across consumer credit, fraud, portfolio risk, and borrower behaviour

 Go beyond the surface level to build sophisticated yet explainable models that connect data to real-world events, customer attitudes and behaviors to deliver insights and inform high-value business decisions

 Flux and current densities
 Dielectric withstand and BIL

 Tap changers and Dual Voltage switches
 Bushings, arrestors and fusing
 Terminal arrangements and type, etc.
 Accessories such as PRDs, gauges, etc.

 Connection diagrams
 Nameplate data

 Bill of materials for electrical components

   Collaboration and Coordination:

 Collaborate with manufacturing, test, and quality teams to resolve non-conformances, implement engineering changes, and validate design improvements.

 3+ years of experience in a designer role in an engineering or manufacturing environment of electrical distribution equipment, preferably transformers.
